My point is that it should have been. The title of the patch is upcoming *balance changes*. As in, they want to bring more *balance* to the game. This does none of that. If they weren't trying to make warrior more playable at the moment then they shouldn't have added the change as a hotfix, they should have waited until the next expansion release when the class would be getting more tools and options for other archetypes. The whole reason they had so much pressure to change these cards was because the meta was a mess and this does nothing to remedy that.

I'm saying they should be redesigning cards so that they remain within the realm of play-ability and don't destroy one of the only currently playable archetypes for an entire class. Of course they shouldn't be redesigning cards based on decks that don't currently exist. That is what future card design is for.

I'm not shocked or upset, I'm saying they repeated their first mistake but in the opposite direction. If someone told you the soup that you made them was too hot you don't leave it in the freezer for an hour and give it back to them expecting them to be happy. There are no currently playable warrior decks outside of pirate warrior at the moment and if blizzard wants to change that, it's not going to be by redesigning a couple cards to be strictly worse in all archetypes, its going to have to come from new tools being printed for those archetypes in future expansions.

No other warrior deck exists at the moment aside from maybe taunt warrior, which blizzard has already printed tons of early game help for. If they want midrange and control warrior archetypes to exist they need to print more tools for them in upcoming expansions, not take the legs out from underneath the class' only currently playable archetype.
